thread:
customer-joe: Hey team, after we switched the prod webapp to use the new interface endpoint (vpce-08f...), our API calls to api.redwood.com started returning 403s and occasional 1.2–1.8s tail latency. This started after the VPC endpoint rollout 2 hours ago. Ticket #12345. Anyone seen this pattern?

maya: Sorry you're hitting this, we'll take a look. Can you paste a curl -v response and the resolver result (dig/getent) from a failing host? Also which subnet (private/public) is the app in?

customer-joe: Paste below — curl shows 403 with x-rw-request-id header: r-7f2a9

```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
* Connected to api.redwood.example.com (34.210.12.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection established
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example.com
> User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< content-type: application/json
< x-rw-request-id: r-7f2a9
< content-length: 89
{ "error": "forbidden", "message": "access denied by policy" }
```

customer-joe: And dig: `dig +short api.redwood.example.com` returns `34.210.12.45` (public IP). We expected this to resolve to the VPCE ENI private IP after enabling Private DNS.

alex: Hmm — if dig returns a public IP then Private DNS probably didn't attach or there's a Route53 split-horizon overlap. Which type of endpoint did you create? An Interface endpoint for a custom service? Did you enable Private DNS on the endpoint?

customer-joe: We created an Interface VPCE to the partner service (com.amazonaws.vpce.some-service) and checked the console. "Enable Private DNS" was ticked. No private hosted zone on our account for that domain.

toni: Two quick possibilities: 1) The domain api.redwood.example.com is a CNAME to a global ALB host that Route53 still resolves to the public ALB IPs for your VPC (split-horizon mismatch). 2) There's a resolver config on the instance overriding DHCP DNS (e.g., custom /etc/hosts or an outbound DNS forwarder hitting public resolver). Also confirm that you don't have an outbound firewall/NAT that rewrites SNI — that can cause backend to reject requests with unmatched host header -> 403.

sam: Also check endpoint policy and per-service access control on our side. If the request comes from an unexpected source (public IP from NAT), our service might reject it. That would explain 403. But if you hit the VPCE ENI IP with Host: api.redwood.example.com we should accept it.

customer-joe: I ran a traceroute and route table dump from a pod:

```
$ ip route show
default via 10.0.0.1 dev eth0 proto static
10.0.0.0/24 dev eth0 proto kernel scope link src 10.0.0.85
# no specific route for 34.210.12.45 (public)
```

And `nslookup api.redwood.example.com` -> 34.210.12.45.

maya: Thanks — those outputs clinch it. Your VPC is still resolving the service domain to the public IP, so traffic leaves via your NAT and hits the public ALB. The request path and client IP differ from what our VPCE expects, so our ingress policy denies. That also explains the higher egress bandwidth/costs you saw post-rollout.

customer-joe: We also saw an unexpected spike on the monthly bill during the 2 hr window, yes.

alex: Root cause checklist: missing/private DNS mismatch OR Route53 association not present -> public resolution. Also check if you have a private hosted zone for the same domain in another account/PHZ association causing split-horizon. Steps to repro locally: from an EC2 in the same subnet do `dig +short api.redwood.example.com` and `curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:10.0.5.12 https://api.redwood.example.com` (replace 10.0.5.12 with VPCE ENI IP) — if direct to ENI succeeds then it's definitely the DNS resolution.

customer-joe: I did the resolve override test and direct-to-ENI works (200). So DNS is the issue.

sre-bot: Automated check: VPCE private-dns status: ENABLED. Route53 resolver rules: none. PHZ associations: none. Detected domain CNAME chain to public ALB.

toni: Fix options (order of recommended actions):
- Option A (recommended): Create/associate a Route53 Private Hosted Zone for api.redwood.example.com pointing to the VPCE ENI private IP (or use the endpoint's private DNS via the VPCE if the service supports it). Ensure the PHZ is associated with the VPCs that need access.
- Option B: If you rely on central resolver or outbound forwarding, add a conditional forwarder to resolve the service domain to the private IPs or enable the VPCE Private DNS in the account owning the domain.
- Option C: As a quick workaround, add an iptables host override or /etc/hosts entry (temporary, not recommended at scale).

sam: Also verify Security Group on the VPCE ENI allows traffic from your app subnets, and check VPCE policy doesn't restrict principal by VPC. If you see 403s from our side tied to policy, we can relax for the rollout while you fix DNS.

customer-joe: We enabled private DNS in the endpoint creation but I see that the domain is a CNAME to an external ALB hostname (service.external-alb.amazonaws.com). Looks like enable-private-dns does not override cross-account PHZ/CNAME mapping. I'll create a PHZ and associate it.

maya: Once you create the PHZ, run the dig test and paste results. We'll keep an eye on request-ids (r-7f2a9) and watch for any more 403s. If you want, we can temporarily whitelist your account/vpc for the request window.

customer-joe: PHZ created and associated with prod VPC. Dig now returns 10.0.5.12. Curl to api.redwood.example.com -> 200, latency back to normal. No further 403s.

maya: Great — marking this resolved. Root cause: split-horizon DNS (public CNAME -> public ALB) + missing private hosted zone association causing traffic to egress via NAT and be rejected by service policy. Action items: customer to keep PHZ association and remove any DNA-level forwarders that bypass VPC DNS. Support to follow up about temporary whitelist if billing spike needs credit.

customer-joe: Thanks everyone. Please add a short KB for "interface endpoint DNS resolves to public IP -> 403" so other customers don't hit this. :pray:
